Loosed by the king, and freed from Egypt’s dungeon,
Lord of the house, made steward of his substance.

He bound his princes: “You must Joseph please;”
Ordered his elders: “Hear the Lord’s decrees.”
Welcomed in Egypt, Israel and his clan,
And Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham.
He made them fruitful, stronger than th’Egyptians,
God turned their hearts to hate and cheat His servants.

Moses His servant, Aaron whom He chose,
God sent to Ham, and mighty signs He shows.
God made it dark, yet they obeyed His word.
God killed their fish in waters turned to blood.
Frogs from the land infested royal chambers.
God ordered flies and lice to swarm their borders.

He gave them hail, and fire rained on their land.
He smote their vines and fig trees with His hand.
He broke in pieces trees within their bounds.
Locusts and nymphs infested all their grounds,
All fruit and vegetation they devoured.
God smote their firstborn, chief of all their pow’r.

God brought them forth with silver and with gold.
Among their tribes none fell beneath the load.
Egypt was glad to watch their fear take flight.
He spread a cloud for shade and fire for light.
Israel asked; God fed them quail and manna,
Opened the rock, the waters gushed like fountains.

His holy promise, made to Abraham,
God to His people kept 43 and brought from Ham
With joy and gladness; 44 They received the lands
Of heathen nations, labors of their hands.
That they observe His statutes, keep His Torah,
Praise ye the LORD, you people! Praise Jehovah!
321:
O thank the LORD, declare His name;
His wondrous deeds to all proclaim.
Sing praise to Him, His works record;
Let all rejoice who seek the LORD.
O seek the LORD, His presence seek!
Remember all His wondrous deeds,
The mighty judgments He declared,
O seed of Abrah’m, Jacob’s heirs.

He is the LORD; He rules the earth,
Remembering His holy Word:
The cov’nant He did e’er command,
The covenant with Abraham,
The promise sure that Isaac heard,
Which unto Jacob He confirmed,
He swore to Israel, “I will give you
Canaan as your heritage.”

When few in number, very few,
They sojourned there while passing through.
They wandered on from land to land,
Through kingdoms on to other clans.
He let none hurt them nor oppress,
He chided kings in their defense:
“Touch not My anointed ones, be warned!
And to My prophets do no harm.”

He summoned famine on their land;
Their food was stopped at His command.
But Joseph, sent ahead of them,
Was sold a slave to ruthless men.
His feet in fetters were confined,
His neck put in a brace of iron.
Till his predictions came to pass,
The LORD’s Word proved him as a test.

The king then sent for his release,
The ruler gave him liberty.
He made him lord of all his lands,
His princes bowed to his commands.
Then Israel came to Egypt’s land,
And Jacob sojourned there in Ham.
The Lord God made His people grow;
He made them stronger than their foe.

He changed their hearts to hate His own,
To plot against His servant’s sons.
And Moses, Aaron then He sent
To Ham to do His signs for them.
He sent deep darkness on the land;
Against His words they did not stand.
He turned their waters into blood,
Which caused their fish to be destroyed.

The frogs filled palaces and homes;
His word caused flies and gnats to swarm.
He sent down hail. Bright lightning flashed.
He struck their vines. Their trees He smashed.
He spoke and countless locusts came,
And all things green grasshoppers ate.
The firstborn of the land He killed,
The firstfruits of their strength and skill.

He brought out Israel, strong and bold,
With Egypt’s silver, jewels and gold.
How glad was Egypt when they left,
For dread of Israel on them fell.
God covered them with cloud by day.
His fire by night to guide their way.
They asked, and He brought quail for them;
He gave them ample bread from heav’n.

He split the rock and water gushed,
Like streams through desert land it rushed.
For He recalled His holy Word,
He swore to Abrah’m long before.
He brought them out with songs of joy,
And gave them lands where others toiled,
That they might keep His holy Word
And heed His statutes. Praise the LORD!
322:
1. Sing praise to the LORD! Oh, thank GOD for His goodness;
His covenant mercy forever endures.
What tongue can declare all the LORD’s deeds and praises?
How blest those who always do justice and right.
Remember me, LORD, when You bless all Your people,
And come to my aid when You save them in grace.
So then I may witness Your chosen ones’ glory,
Share joy with Your nation, with Your people praise.

2. We’ve sinned like our fathers, done wrong; we are guilty;
Our fathers in Egypt did not heed Your signs.
They did not remember Your covenant mercy,
But at the Red Sea they rebelled against God.
And yet, for His name’s sake He saved them, showed greatness;
The Red Sea He also rebuked and made dry.
He led them through depths as one walks through the desert,
And saved them from foes, and redeemed them in pow’r.

3. Their enemies drowned and there were no survivors;
So His word they trusted, and His praises sang.
But soon they forgot it, did not wait for counsel;
They craved in the desert, put God to the test.
He heeded their pleading and gave what they wanted,
But then He sent on them a wasting disease.
Yet then, where they camped, they grew jealous of Moses,
And also of Aaron, the LORD’s holy priest.

4. The earth split wide open, and swallowed up Dathan,
And over Abiram’s whole faction it closed;
Then fire blazed on those who had followed their counsel,
And these wicked people were burned in the flames.
At Horeb they worshiped a calf of their making;
Their glory exchanged for an ox that eats grass,
Forgot God their Savior, His great deeds in Egypt,
His wonders, His exploits beside the Red Sea.

5. He said He’d destroy them, but His chosen Moses
Stepped into the breach and deflected His wrath.
But then they despised the good land He had promised,
They did not believe all the word that He gave,
Complained in their tents and ignored the LORD’s speaking.
So He swore He’d make them in wilderness fall.
He’d scatter their children among all the nations,
Dispersing them over the face of the earth.

6. The Baal of Peor was the one whom they followed;
They ate sacrifices to gods that are dead.
Provoking God’s anger, a plague He sent on them,
Till Phinehas rose up: the plague was then stayed.
This action so righteous is ever remembered.
Yet they angered Him at the Meribah springs.
So Moses had trouble: He spoke to them rashly;
For they had resisted the Spirit of God.

7. They did not destroy all the peoples God ordered,
But mixed with the Gentiles and followed their ways.
They bowed to their idols; this was their undoing:
To demons their children as sacrifice gave.
They shed blood of innocent sons and of daughters,
When they sacrificed to the Canaanite gods.
The land and 39 the people were unclean through evil;
The LORD showed His wrath and His people He loathed.

8. He gave them to kings of the heathen who crushed them;
Though He often freed them yet still they rebelled.
For He had regard to their cry; In His cov’nant
He showed them His grace, made their captors be kind.
So save us, LORD God, bring us back from the heathen;
We’ll boast in Your praise and Your holy name thank.
The LORD God of Israel be blessed forever.
All people of God say, “Amen.” Praise the LORD!
323:
Oh, praise the LORD! Oh, thank the LORD,
For bountiful is He;
Because His lovingkindness lasts
Through all eternity.
Oh, who can fully praise the LORD,
Or count His deeds of might?
How blest are they who justice keep,
And always do what’s right.

Remember me with favor, LORD,
Which You Your people show.
O come to me, draw near that I
May Your salvation know;
That with Your chosen ones I may
Enjoy prosperity,
And may with Your inheritance
In You boast joyfully.

With all our fathers we have sinned;
We have done wickedly.
Our fathers did not understand
Your signs in Egypt seen;
Though they Your acts of love forgot,
And at the Sea rebelled,
He saved them still, for His name’s sake;
His power they beheld.

The Red Sea dried at His rebuke;
He led them on dry land.
He saved them from their hostile foes,
Redeemed them from their hand.
The waters drowned their enemies,
Not one of them remained.
His people then believed His words,
His praise in song proclaimed.

His people soon forgot His works,
Did not wait for His will;
But lusted in the wilderness,
And God they tested still.
He filled them with the meat they craved,
A plague made their reward.
Men envied Moses, Aaron scorned—
One holy to the LORD.

The opened earth on Dathan closed,
Abiram’s kin entombed.
A fire blazed in their company
And wicked ones consumed.
And they at Horeb forged a calf,
Before its image kneeled;
Exchanged their Glory for an ox
That grazes in the field.

Then God their Savior they forgot,
In Egypt His great deeds;
His wonders in the land of Ham,
Signs by the Sea of Reeds.
And so He said He would destroy
If Moses, His elect,
Stood not before Him in the breach,
His anger to deflect.

Then they despised the pleasant land,
Did not believe His word.
Instead they grumbled in their tents,
And disobeyed the LORD.
He therefore vowed to cast them down,
There in the desert sands,
Among the nations cast their seed,
And scatter through the lands.

With Ba’al Peor they had joined,
Ate off’rings to the dead.
They stirred His anger with their deeds;
The plague among them spread.
The plague was stopped when Phinehas
Arose and intervened.
This was accounted righteousness
Through all eternity.

At Meribah they angered Him,
On Moses grief they brought;
For they provoked his spirit there;
His speech was rash and hot.
They did not heed the LORD’s command
That peoples should be slain;
Instead they mingled in their land,
Learned practices profane.

They worshiped other foreign gods,
Became ensnared by these;
They burned their sons and daughters up
The demons to appease.
The blood of daughters and of sons—
Blood of their guiltless child—
Was sacrificed to Canaan’s gods;
The land became defiled.

The people thus became unclean,
Defiled within their heart;
For in their deeds and practices
They played the harlot’s part.
And so against His people burned
The anger of the LORD;
Then His own people He despised,
His heritage abhorred.

God put His tribes in foreign hands,
Those hating them had rule.
And they were subjugated by
Their enemies so cruel.
Though often He delivered them,
They always turned from Him;
And following their evil plan,
Sank deeper yet in sin.

Yet their distress He looked upon,
Their cry to Him was heard.
And He recalled His covenant,
For their sake kept His word.
Then He relented in His grace,
And for His mercy’s sake.
He caused their captors to relent
And on them pity take.

Deliver us, O LORD our God;
From foreign lands reclaim,
That we may glory in Your praise
And thank Your holy name.
The LORD be blest, yes, Israel’s God,
Through all eternity.
O people, praise the LORD and say,
“Amen! Yes, let it be.”
324:
Give thanks to God, rejoicing
Because the LORD is good.
Bless Him with anthems voicing
Your love and gratitude.
He who our peace ensures
Forsakes His promise never.
His steadfast love endures,
And we are His forever.

Let all this be repeated;
Let those whom He set free
Retell how He defeated
Their fiercest enemy.
He gave them peace and rest.
In far-off lands He sought them;
From east as well as west,
From north and south He brought them.

Some, wand’ring in waste places,
Found nowhere they could stay.
God heard them and was gracious;
He led them on their way.
With thirst and hunger weak,
They cried to God to save them
From deserts dry and bleak.
A place of rest He gave them.

God led them to a city
Where they could safely dwell;
He showed them love and pity.
Let them His wonders tell,
And let their anthems rise.
His steadfast love relieves them.
Their thirst He satisfies;
No more their hunger grieves them.

Some, chained in gloomy prisons,
Endured His anger’s rod.
They had rebelled and risen
Against the words of God.
His counsel they had spurned,
The Most High’s voice neglected.
In vain for help they yearned;
They were by all rejected.

They cried to GOD to save them;
He broke their shackles all
And liberty He gave them;
The gloom did He dispel.
Let them God’s love adore
And at His marvels wonder;
He shatters great bronze doors,
Snaps iron bars asunder.

Some were with illness stricken
Because of sin and guilt.
All food caused them to sicken;
They were with loathing filled.
Close to death’s gates they came,
And there were none to cheer them.
Then in their grief and shame
They cried, and God did hear them.

To them His Word revealing,
He came with pow’r to save,
Stretched out His hand of healing
And snatched them from the grave.
Let them all thank the LORD,
Their sacrifices bringing,
And His great deeds record
With joyful shouts and singing.

Some who in ships were sailing
The ocean’s mighty sweep
Saw there God’s pow’r prevailing
In wonders of the deep.
The tempest, when He spoke,
Caused waves to rise like mountains
That roared and fell and broke
Into wild, foaming fountains.

10. They were distressed and humbled;
Their courage ebbed away.
Like drunken men they stumbled
In terror and dismay.
The LORD saw their despair,
And when to Him they shouted,
He heard their fervent pray’r;
The raging storm He routed.

11. The LORD, their fears allaying,
Bade storm and wind be still;
Hushed were the waves, obeying
Their Maker’s word and will.
How happy were the men
When He the calm provided
And He their ship again
To longed-for havens guided.

Let all then thank their Savior
With shouts of joyful praise,
Extol His love and favor,
Shown in such wondrous ways.
Let them break out in song
Within their congregation.
Let Him be praised among
The elders of the nation.

Into dry land He changes
The fields where streams abound.
Clear springs and verdant ranges
He turns to thirsty ground.
To salty wastes He turned
A land of fruit and flower
Because its people spurned
His words of truth and power.

Into cool streams He changes
A thirsty desert land.
In parched and barren ranges
Flow springs at His command.
There He reveals His grace,
Shows hungry ones His pity,
Allows them in that place
To build themselves a city.

He grants them fields for sowing
And vineyards to prepare;
In harvests overflowing
They see God’s wondrous care.
His favor does not cease;
Their garners they replenish.
In number they increase;
Their herds do not diminish.

God pours contempt on princes
When they His own oppress,
Drives them with their pretenses
Into the wilderness.
He, lifting them from woe,
His people does remember;
Like flocks their fam’lies grow,
For He adds to their number.

The upright with elation
God’s mighty works acclaim;
The wicked of all nations
Are silent, put to shame.
Let then the wise regard
All this with awe and wonder,
And, turning to the LORD,
Let them His mercy ponder.
325:
Oh, glorify Him, for the LORD, He is good;
Forever is His cov’nant love.
Let those that the LORD has redeemed make it known—
Redeemed from the hand of the foe.
For He took them out of the lands where they were,
And brought them together again,
From regions that lay to the east and the west,
From those to the north and the south.

They wandered through wilderness, desert and waste;
No city to live in was found.
They suffered from hunger, they suffered from thirst;
Their soul grew exhausted and weak.
And then in their trouble they cried to the LORD
Because of the peril they faced;
And out from the dangers and troubles they knew
He brought them to safety at last.

A right way He led them until they had found
A city, a true dwelling place.
For this reason let them give thanks to the LORD,
Because of His covenant love—
Because of the great things that He brings about,
Things done for the sons of mankind.
For He quenched the thirst of the soul that was parched,
The hungering soul filled with good.

Yet some lived in darkness, in shadow of death,
As prisoners wretched and chained,
Because they rebelled against what God had said;
The Most High’s good counsel they spurned.
And so He has humbled their heart with hard toil;
They stumbled but no one would help.
Then they in their trouble cried out to the LORD;
He rescued them from their distress.

From darkness He brought them, from shadow of death;
And He broke their shackles apart.
For this reason let them give thanks to the LORD,
Because of His covenant love,
Because of the great things that He brings about,
Things done for the sons of mankind.
For He broke the mightiest gates made of bronze,
And cut through their strong iron bars.

Yet fools were afflicted because they rebelled,
Because of their ungodly ways.
Their soul felt abhorrence for all kinds of food,
And up to death’s gates they drew near.
In trouble severe they cried out to the LORD;
He rescued them from their distress.
He sent forth His word and re stored them to health,
And saved them from ruin and death.

Oh, let them give thanks for the LORD’s gracious love,
The wonders He does for mankind.
So let them present sacrifices of thanks,
And tell of His deeds in glad song.
326:
All those who go down to the sea in their ships,
Who sail the great waters for trade,
They too have beheld what the LORD has done there,
His wonderful acts in the deep.

He spoke and commanded a great storm of wind
That lifted the waves of the sea.
They rose to the heav’ns, then dropped down to the depths.
The souls of men melted with fear.

They reeled and they staggered like men who were drunk.
Their wisdom had all fled away.
Then they in their trouble cried out to the LORD;
He rescued them from their distress.

The storm wind He settled and caused to be still;
The waves of the sea became calm.
The sailors were glad when the waves had died down,
And to a safe haven He led.

Oh, let them give thanks for the LORD’s gracious love,
The wonders He does for mankind.
When people are gathered, oh, let them give praise,
And hail Him where elders convene.
327:
Some rivers He changes to desert and waste,
And water-springs to arid ground.
A land that is fruitful He turns into salt,
For evil were those living there.
Yet wilderness then He can turn into pools,
From desert can make water-springs.
He makes such a place for the hungry to dwell,
To set up a city as home.

They then may sow seeds and plant vineyards and fields,
And gather a plentiful yield.
He blesses them greatly, their numbers increase;
He’ll not let their cattle decrease.
But when they were few, they were bowed and brought low
From hardship, oppression, and grief;
On princes He pours out His scorn, so they roam
In wastelands without any path.

But safe from affliction He raises the poor,
To set them securely on high.
And families, too, He will treat with His care,
And make them to be like a flock.
The upright will see this, and as they rejoice,
All wrongdoing closes its mouth.
Is anyone wise? Let him hold to these things,
And think on the LORD’s gracious love.
328:
Those who go down to the sea in ships
Do business in great waters,
They all have seen Jehovah’s works,
His wonders in deep waters,
For He spoke and He raised up a stormy wind,
Which lifted up seawaters.
They skyward lunged, then deep down plunged,
Into the waves of water.

In misery their souls did melt,
They reeled like drunken sailors,
Their wisdom all was swallowed up
They came to their wit’s ending.
Then they cried to Jehovah in their great need,
He brought them out of trouble.
He caused all the storm-winds to quiet down.
He hushed the ocean-waters.

In misery their souls did melt,
They reeled like drunken sailors,
Their wisdom all was swallowed up
They came to their wit’s ending.
Then they cried to Jehovah in their great need,
He brought them out of trouble.
He made all the storm winds to quiet down.
He hushed the ocean-waters.

Then they rejoiced on a quiet sea,
He led them to their haven.
Let them give thanks to Jehovah God,
For all His loving mercy.
For the wonders He does for the sons of men,
Let sailors all extol Him.
In the congregation where people meet,
Praise Him with seated elders.
329:
My Heart, O God, Is Resolute!

My heart, O God, is resolute!
I will sing forth Your praises.
Awake, my glory! Harp and lute!
I sing; the dawn awakens.
O LORD, I sing among the tribes;
My song to You all strength ascribes.
I’ll praise among the nations.

Your mercy’s great above the sky,
Your truth ascends to heaven.
Arise, O God, above the sky;
Your splendor o’er creation;
That Your beloved be set free,
Hold out Your strong right hand to me;
Respond and grant salvation.

God answered in His holiness,
“I will rejoice in triumph;
The lot of Shechem I assess,
And judge the Vale of Succoth.
The land of Gilead is Mine,
I claim Manasseh, too, as Mine;
And Ephraim is My helmet.

4. “While Judah is My lawyer-king,
Yet Moab is my soap dish;
My shoe, o’er Edom, I will fling;
Philistia I vanquish.”
Now who will give me safe resort?
Or lead me into Edom’s fort?
Did You not let us languish?

5. Was it not You who sent us out
But did not join our forces?
Provide us help from trouble now!
The help of man is useless.
Through God we will do valiantly,
For He shall win our victory,
He’ll trample our distresses.
330:
1. That Your beloved may be spared,
Save us and hear our pleading.
In holiness have You declared:
“Exult in Me exceeding!”
All nations west and east,
The greatest to the least,
From south to north are all
Your portion when You call:
Let praise arise exceeding.

2. Who now shall lead against our foes
When God has left us falt’ring?
Lord, You have left us in our woes,
Our foes o’er us exalting.
Grant strength to win the day!
Lord, help us in the way!
The strength of man is vain
The victory to gain:
But Jesus is not halting.
331:
My steadfast heart, O God,
Will sound Thy praise abroad
With tuneful string;
The dawn shall hear my song,
Thy praise I will prolong,
And where Thy people throng
Thanksgiving bring.

Thy truth and tender love
Are high as heav’n above;
Thy help we crave.
Be Thou exalted high
Above the lofty sky;
Lest Thy beloved die,
Oh, hear and save.

God’s Word shall surely stand;
His name through ev’ry land
Shall be adored;
Lord, who shall lead our host?
Thy aid we covet most,
In Thee is all our boast,
Strong in the Lord.
332:
O God of all my praise,
Number these painful days.
The hearts of all these wicked men
Tell lies with tongue and pen.

2. They open mouths to lie;
Their hearts are proud and high.
They compass me with words of hate,
Leave me disconsolate.

No reason for their bile;
No sense in being vile.
I prayed for them; look what they did,
Their lies in cesspool hid.

For all my good they bent,
And love on hatred spent.
My kindness to them twisted back
And showed the love they lack.

Let him a tyrant serve,
And charges thick deserve.
When he is judged, let guilt pour in.
And let his pray’r be sin.

So let his days be few;
His years on earth as dew.
His office let another take,
His bishopric forsake.

His children orphans be,
His wife a widow, free
Of living with a wretched man
Throughout a tedious span.

And let them beg for bread,
With rags upon the head,
In desolation let them scrape,
And never find escape.

Then let extortion come,
And take his cursed home.
Let strangers spoil and never shirk;
Let plunder do its work.

May mercy not appear
To quell his rising fear.
Let no one come to grace his line,
His lineage decline.

Appoint his fathers’ sins
Where sentencing begins.
His mother’s sins be reckoned here
And never wash it clear.

With righteous judgment planned
So let his sin still stand,
That You may blot from memory
His name eternally.

He would not mercy show,
Nor into kindness go.
To persecute the destitute,
His foul desires he suits.

He loved the vi’lent curse,
He strove to make it worse—
So let it fall the same on him,
With retribution grim.

He did not love to bless—
His hatred measureless—
He put on curses like a cloak,
So may he on them choke.

His cursing turn to groans,
Like oil  in his bones,
Like water in his inward parts
In choking fits and starts.
333:
Let this be from the LORD,
My enemy’s reward,
For those who speak against my soul,
Whose hatred takes its toll.

My heartfelt wound is deep,
My poverty I keep,
For I am gone like shadows go.
Like locusts when they blow.

I fast, my knees give way,
I can’t make fatness stay.
As those who see me shake their head,
I writhe upon my bed.

So help me, GOD and Lord,
Save me by Your own Word.
That they may know this is Your hand,
My salvation You planned.

So let them curse; You bless
In joy and righteousness.
Let all their words bring them to grief,
Bring low with no relief.

And I will praise the LORD,
His kindnesses record,
In the assembly of the just,
I sing because I must.

For God will righteous stand
At poverty’s right hand,
To save me from the cursing one,
He saves; His work is done.
334:
O God, I praise You, do not silent be!
For wicked, crafty mouths opened at me.
They spoke against me with mouths that create
Lies, 3 and surrounded me with words of hate.
They fought against me with no good excuse;
I gave them love but they chose to accuse.

2. But I am praying now. 5 They have repaid
My good with evil; hate for love I gave.
Set up a wicked man him to command.
Let his accuser be at his right hand.
When he is judged, let him be found guilty,
Let all his pray’rs become iniquity.

Give someone else his place! Shorten his life!
Make his kids fatherless! Widow his wife!
Yes, let his children be beggars that roam
Far from the rubble of their ruined homes.
Let his belongings be all repossessed.
Let strangers rob him of all he has earned.

Let there be none to show kindness to him.
None to give grace to his fatherless kin.
Cut off the name of his posterity.
Blot them all out of the world’s memory.
Let all his father’s sins come to the LORD,
His mother’s wickedness ever record.
335:
O God of my praise, don’t ignore me in silence!
The lies of the wicked oppose me with torments.
Their tongues have attacked me with cruel accusation.
They’ve circled around me with words of revulsion;
They’ve turned without cause and become my assailants
Betraying my love, they’ve become my opponents.

2. I have no resort but this pray’r to my Father!
My good they despise and reward me with anger,
My love they deride with a hateful aggression.
So give him a king that will rule with oppression,
And let accusations be brought by his rival.
Condemn him for sin; let his pray’r become evil.

Let death take him soon; give his place to another.
His children abandon, alone without father,
His wife make a widow without a protector.
Make beggars and tramps of his son and his daughter
And let them seek bread straying far from their hovels.
Let creditors rob him despite how he grovels.

4. Let strangers extort all the fruit of his labor.
Let none show him mercy, nor act as his neighbor;
Do not let his fatherless sons be shown pity.
Cut off his descendants; expelled from the city,
In one generation their honor be wasted:
Let hist’ry forget that he ever existed!

Recall ev’ry evil his fathers committed,
See none of the crimes of his mother acquitted.
Expose all their sin to Jehovah forever,
So blot from the earth ev’ry thought of his favor.
Because he forgot to relieve the forsaken,
But tortured the needy and slaughtered the broken.

As he loved to curse, overwhelm him with cursing;
As he would not bless, let him never find blessing.
His garment was cursing he wore with approval,
So make it his belt with no hope of removal.
Let all who malign me have this condemnation;
Reward them in kind for their false accusation.
336:
But, O sovereign LORD, in mercy
Deal with me for Your name’s sake;
Save me in Your love and goodness,
And my life from danger take.

For I am both poor and needy;
Crushed with in me is my heart.
I am feeble, like an insect;
Like a shadow I depart.

See, my knees give way from fasting;
And my frame is thin and gaunt.
My accusers, when they see me,
Shake their heads at me and taunt.

LORD my God, draw near and help me;
Save me in Your steadfast love.
Let them know Your hand has done it,
That my help comes from above.

They may curse, but You will bless me,
And Your servant will give praise.
Clothed with shame be my accusers,
My attackers with disgrace.

I will loudly sing God’s praises,
And extol Him in the throng;
For He helps and saves the needy
From all those who do them wrong.
337:
Jehovah to my Lord has said,
“Sit Thou at My right hand
Until I make Thy foes a stool
Whereon Thy feet may stand.”
Jehovah shall from Zion send
The scepter of Thy pow’r.
In battle with Thine enemies
Be Thou the conqueror.

A willing people in Thy day
Of pow’r shall come to Thee.
Thy youth arrayed in holiness
Like morning dew shall be.
Jehovah swore, and from His oath
He never will depart:
“Of th’order of Melchizedek
A priest Thou ever art.”

The Lord at Thy right hand shall smite
Earth’s rulers in His wrath.
Among the nations He shall judge;
The slain shall fill His path.
In many lands He’ll overthrow
Their kings with ruin dread;
And, marching, He’ll drink from the brook
And so lift up His head.
338:
Yahweh to my Lord hath spoken,
“Sit Thee down at My right hand
Till I make Thy foes a footstool
Whereupon Thy feet may stand.”
Yahweh forth shall send Thee;
Zion aid shall lend Thee.
With the scepter of Thy pow’r
Be Thou now the conqueror.

In Thy day of pow’r shall praise Thee
People clothed in bright array;
Eagerly they come before Thee
At Thy feet their lives to lay.
Bright as early morning,
Righteous deeds adorning,
Shining as the dew at dawn
Is Thine awesome bannered throng!

Yahweh swore, repents He never;
From His oath He’ll not depart.
“Of the order of Melchiz’dek
Everlasting priest Thou art.”
Yahweh has appointed:
Christ is the anointed
Of the Father; at His hand,
Furiously He strikes the land.

He doth judge among the nations,
And the slain shall fill His path.
He did crush the head of Satan;
Ruined kings shall feel His wrath.
Ev’ry foe is vanquished!
All His work accomplished
Drinking from the royal stream
Lifts His head, our righteous King.
339:
The LORD to my Lord has said, “Sit at My right hand,
Till I make all Your enemies Your footstool.”
Out of Zion Jehovah will stretch Your scepter forth,
Saying, “Rule in the midst of Your foes.”

Your people will come freely in Your mighty day,
Each arrayed in His holy apparel.
From the womb of the morning Your volunteers will come,
And Your young men appear like the dew.

Jehovah has sworn and He will not change His mind:
“You’re a Priest in Melchizedek’s order.”
At Your right hand Jehovah will shatter many kings,
When the day of His anger arrives.

He will judge in the nations and fill them with the dead.
He will shatter the chiefs of a great land.
He will drink from the stream flowing right beside the road,
And so He will lift up His head.
340:
Praise to the LORD! I will extol Him
While gathering with the upright.
Great are the works of GOD, and pondered
By all who in them take delight.

His deeds are glorious and majestic;
His righteousness endures always.
He caused His works to be remembered;
Kind is the LORD and full of grace.

Food He provides for those who fear Him;
His covenant for ever stands.
His mighty works He showed His people
By giving them the nations’ lands.

Faithful and just are all His actions;
All His commands are faithful too,
Steadfast for ever and for ever.
The works of God are right and true.

He sent redemption for His people;
His covenant remains the same,
Ordained by Him throughout all ages—
Holy and awesome is His name.

Fear of the LORD gives rise to wisdom;
All those who walk in upright ways
Have insight and good understanding.
To Him belongs eternal praise.
341:
Praise the LORD with exaltation,
My whole heart my LORD shall praise;
With the ransomed congregation
Worthy hallelujahs raise.

All His works are great and glorious,
Saints review them with delight;
His redemption all victorious
We remember day and night.

Strength He gives to those who fear Him,
Of His cov’nant mindful still;
Wise they are who much revere Him,
And rejoice to do His will.

For His grace stands fast forever,
His decrees the saints secure;
From His oath He turneth never,
Ev’ry promise standeth sure.

Therefore be His praise unceasing,
Be His name for ever blest;
And with confidence increasing,
Let us on His promise rest.
343:
The man of reverence to God
Is blessed in the highest class;
His ready feet with joy are shod,
To bring the word to pass.
His seed shall mighty pow’r invest.
And gain on earth the first repute,
And all the branches shall be blest
Of such a faithful root.

His soul shall have her full repast
Of wealth and earth’s abundant store.
And his integrity shall last
In Heav’n for evermore.
The good mid Satan’s dark domain
The dayspring has before his view,
Such are benevolent in grain,
And loving, kind and true.

A good man is a common friend,
And in all characters complete.
He will be merciful to lend,
And in his words discreet.
For he shall never change his side,
But still keep steadfast and the same,
And God the honest man shall guide
To sempiternal fame.

His spirit shall not be dismayed
At evil tidings unawares.
And his firm heart to Christ his aid
Submits his soul’s affairs.
His heart no alteration knows,
Nor is from God to Belial waved;
And his desire upon his foes
Is that they should be saved.

His worldly goods unto the poor
He hath distributed around;
His worth for ever shall endure
In exaltation crowned.
The wicked shall behold his rise.
And learn and imitate his ways,
Till all their envy, all their vice
Subside in pray’r and praise.
344:
Praise the LORD, all you who fear Him;
Blest are all who love His Word.
Mighty are the upright children
Of the blessed of the LORD.
Wealth and riches shall not fail them,
Long their righteousness endures.
Light in darkness shall avail them
In God’s grace and mercy sure.

He who is a gracious giver
And who in God’s justice lives,
From His righteous ways shall never
Be removed, but ever thrive.
Bad news shall not leave them fearing:
Firm their hearts who trust in God.
Strong and steady, e’er appearing,
They upon their foes have trod.

Let us then our gen’rous off’rings
To the poor and needy give.
Thus our horn shall be exalted
And our goodness ever live.
Let the wicked see and tremble,
Let them gnash their teeth in rage;
Their desire shall surely crumble
In God’s coming glorious age.
345:
Praise the LORD! O praise Him,
All who know His name!
From this day forever,
Magnify His fame!
From the time each morning
When the sun is raised
To its evening waning,
Let His name be praised!

High above the nations,
On Your glorious throne,
Who is like You, Savior,
Ruling all You own?
sovereign and all-knowing,
Over all above,
Praise to You is owing
For Your perfect love!

Though You rule from heaven,
Looking down on earth,
Praise and thanks be given
To Your holy worth!
Down You reach to touch us,
Clad in ash and dust,
Raising us with such as
In Your favor trust.

Seated now with princes
’Round Your glorious throne,
We by grace are lifted
To become Your own.
Barren women, joyous,
Glad their children bear;
Joining in the chorus,
They Your praise declare.
346:
Hallelujah! Raise, O raise
To the LORD our song of praise!
Praise, O servants of the LORD,
Praise the name of God our LORD!

Blessed be forevermore
That great name which we adore.
Dawn to dusk, from east to west,
Let the LORD’s great name be blest.

O’er all nations God alone,
Higher than the heav’ns His throne,
Who is like the LORD Most High,
Gazing down on earth and sky?

From the dust He lifts the poor,
From the ashes those forlorn;
Those He’s raised up from the pit
With His people’s princes sit.

He the barren woman takes,
And a joyful mother makes
She finds joy in His reward.
Hallelujah! Praise the LORD!
347:
1. When Israel, freed from Pharaoh’s hand,
Left the proud tyrant and his land,
The tribes with cheerful homage own
Their King, and Judah was His throne.

2. Across the deep their journey lay;
The deep divides to make them way:
The Jordan saw their march, and fled
With current backward to his head.

3. The mountains shook like frightened sheep,
Like lambs the little hillocks leap;
Not Sinai on her base could stand,
Conscious of sovereign pow’r at hand.

4. What pow’r could make the deep divide
Make Jordan back ward roll his tide?
Why did ye leap, ye little hills?
And whence the fright that Sinai feels?

5. Let ev’ry mountain, ev’ry flood,
Retire, and know th’approaching God,
The King of Israel: see Him here;
Tremble, thou earth, adore and fear.

6. He thunders, and all nature mourns.
The rock to standing pools He turns;
Flints spring with fountains at His word,
And fires and seas confess the Lord.
348:
When Israel had from Egypt gone,
Jacob from men of speech unknown;
Then Judah was His holy place,
And His dominion Israel’s race.

The sea, affrighted, saw and fled;
Back Jordan driven was with dread;
The lofty mountains skipped like rams,
And all the little hills like lambs.

What ailed thee, that thou fledd’st, O sea?
Thou, Jordan, that thou back didst flee?
Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams?
And all ye little hills like lambs?

Tremble, O earth! The Lord is near:
Before the God of Jacob, fear;
Who from the rock didst water bring,
And made the flint a water spring.
349:
LORD, not to us, O not to us—
To Your name be the praise,
Because Your love and faithfulness
Endure, O LORD, always.

Why do the nations question us?
“Where is their God?” they say.
Our God inhabits heaven high
And over all holds sway.

Their gold and silver images
Are crafted carefully,
But they have mouths which cannot speak,
And eyes which cannot see.

Their noses have no sense of smell;
Their ears can hear no sound.
They have no feeling in their hands,
Nor can they walk around.

5. Although these idols do have throats,
No word can they proclaim.
Their makers and their worshippers
Will all become like them.

O house of Israel, place your trust
Upon the LORD alone;
He is the mighty help and shield
Of all who are His own.

O house of Aaron, trust the LORD;
He is their help and shield.
All you who fear Him, trust the LORD;
He is your help and shield.

The LORD remembers Israel
And He will bless us all—
The house of Aaron and all those
Who fear Him, great and small.

May God the LORD make you increase—
Both you and all your line.
May you be blest by GOD, who makes
All things by His design.

The highest heavens are the LORD’s;
The earth to us He gave.
Dead people do not praise the LORD;
They’re silent in the grave.

But we extol the LORD on high,
His majesty proclaim.
Both now and evermore exalt
And praise His holy name!
350:
Not to our names, Thou only just and true,
Not to our worthless names is glory due;
Thy pow’r and grace, Thy truth and justice, claim
Immortal honors to Thy sovereign name:
Shine through the earth from Heav’n, Thy blest abode,
Nor let the heathens say, “Where is your God?”

Heav’n is Thy higher court, there stands Thy throne,
And through the lower worlds Thy will is done.
Our God framed all this earth, these heav’ns He spread.
But fools adore the gods their hands have made:
The kneeling crowd, with looks devout, behold
Their silver saviors, and their saints of gold.

Vain are those artful shapes of eyes and ears;
The molten image neither sees nor hears;
Their hands are helpless, nor their feet can move,
They have no speech, nor thought, nor pow’r, nor love;
Yet foolish mortals make their long complaints
To their deaf idols and unmoving saints.

4. The rich have statues well adorned with gold;
The poor, content with gods of coarser mould,
With tools of iron carve the senseless stock,
Lopped from a tree, or broken from a rock;
People and priest drive on the solemn trade,
And trust the gods that saws and hammers made.

5. Be heav’n and earth amazed! ’Tis hard to say
Which is more stupid: their false gods or they.
O Israel, trust the Lord; He hears and sees,
He knows thy sorrows and restores thy peace;
His worship does a thousand comforts yield,
He is thy help; He is thy Heav’nly shield.

In God we trust; our impious foes in vain
Attempt our ruin, and oppose His reign;
Had they prevailed, darkness had closed our days,
And death and silence had forbade His praise.
But we are saved, and live— let songs arise
And Zion bless the God that built the skies.
351:
Not unto us, LORD, no, not us,
But to Your name above,
Bring glory for Your faithfulness
And for Your steadfast love.

Why should the heathen nations say,
“Why does their God keep still?”
For our God lives in heaven high,
And carries out His will.

The LORD has kept us in His thoughts;
And He will bless us still.
He’ll bless the house of Israel,
Bless Aaron’s house as well.

He’ll bless all those who fear the LORD,
The great as well as small.
O may the LORD still prosper you,
You and your children all.

May you have blessing from the LORD,
Who made the skies and land.
The highest heavens are the LORD’s,
But earth He gave to man.

The dead are silent in the grave,
They cannot praise the LORD;
But we’ll forever bless the LORD.
Give praises to the LORD!
352:
I love the LORD, the fount of life and grace;
He heard my voice, my cry and supplication,
Inclined His ear, gave strength and consolation;
In life, in death, my heart will seek His face.

The cords of death held me in deep despair;
The terrors of the grave caused me to languish;
I suffered untold grief and bitter anguish;
In my distress I turned to God in pray’r.

3. I cried to Him, “Oh, I beseech Thee, LORD,
Preserve my life and prove Thyself my Savior!”
The LORD is just and He shows grace and favor;
In boundless mercy He fulfills His word.

The LORD preserves the helpless graciously;
For, when brought low, in Him I found salvation.
Come, O my soul, relieved from tribulation,
Turn to your rest; the LORD has favored me.

O righteous LORD, Thou in Thy sovereign grace
Hast saved my soul from death and woe appalling,
Dried all my tears and kept my feet from falling,
That I may live and walk before Thy face.

I have believed, and therefore did I speak
When I was made to suffer tribulation;
I said in haste and bitter consternation:
“All men are false; deceitful ways they seek.”

What shall I render to my Savior now
For all the riches of His consolation?
With joy I’ll take the cup of His salvation,
And call upon His name with thankful vow.

In all His people’s presence I will pay
My vows to Him, the LORD so good and gracious.
To God the death of all His saints is precious;
In times of grief He is their help and stay.

I am, O LORD, Thy servant, bound yet free,
Thy handmaid’s son, whose shackles Thou hast broken.
Redeemed by grace, I’ll render as a token
Of gratitude my constant praise to Thee.

Jerusalem! Within your courts I’ll praise
The LORD’s great name, and with a spirit lowly
Pay all my vows. O Zion, fair and holy,
Come join with me and bless Him all your days!
353:
1. 1–3 I love the LORD because He hears
My cries and pleas for mercy.
Because He bends to me His ears,
My pray’rs shall ever thus be.
The snares of death encompassed me;
Hell’s grip could not unloosened be;
Distress and anguish pressed me.

2. 4–6 I called to GOD, “O LORD, I pray,
Redeem my soul with favor!”
The LORD is gracious in His way,
And righteous is our Savior.
His mercy to the simple flies;
He lifted me up to the skies—
I rest in Him forever!

3. 7–9 Full well the LORD has dealt with me;
My soul from death delivered.
My weeping eyes, my stumbling feet,
He has redeemed forever.
Forever I before His face
Shall walk with those who know His grace,
And dwell with them forever.

4. 10–14 Afflicted, I believe His Word,
Though lying men undo me.
What shall I render to the LORD
For all His blessings to me?
Salvation’s cup I lift above
And call up on the God of love
And pay my vows most truly.

5. 15–19 How sweet to Him when saints depart—
Save me, Your servant, Savior!
From sin You loosed my wand’ring heart;
I praise Your name forever!
On You I call, my vows to pay;
Here in Your presence I would stay
Your praise to offer ever.
354:
Praise the LORD, all ye nations: praise Him, all ye people.
For His merciful kindness is great toward us:
and the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Praise ye the LORD!
Praise ye the LORD!
Praise ye the LORD!
355:
O praise the LORD, all you Gentiles!
And laud Him, all you peoples!
For His merciful kindness is great toward us,
And the truth of the LORD is forever.
Praise the LORD!
356:
Praise ye the LORD, praise ye the LORD!
All nations, peoples, all the earth,
Extol Him, praise Him ev’ryone,
Through ev’ry land by ev’ry tongue.
Great is His steadfast love toward us,
And ever faithful is our God.
The LORD is faithful evermore.
Praise ye the LORD, praise ye the LORD!
358:
O come with thanks, God’s goodness praising;
His firm and steadfast love endures.
2,3 Let Israel and the house of Aaron
Proclaim His love forever sure.
Let all who come to Him in worship
Be in His steadfast love secure.
Come to the LORD with your thanksgiving;
His everlasting love endures.

I cried to God in my affliction;
He answered me and set me free.
The LORD Himself is my protection.
What can a man then do to me?
On all my foes I look in triumph;
With God I face them fearlessly.
8,9 I’ll put no confidence in princes;
The LORD, He shall my refuge be.

I was surrounded by all nations,
But I subdued them in His name;
11,12 And though they swarmed like bees around me,
I beat them down like thorns aflame.
I was hard-pressed and close to falling;
To my support the LORD then came.
He is my song and my salvation;
His strength is evermore the same.

Hear in the dwelling of the righteous
Their joyful songs of victory:
“The LORD’s right hand is high exalted,
The LORD’s right hand does valiantly!”
I shall not die, but live, and praise Him;
In song His deeds my theme shall be.
Although the LORD has sorely chastened,
He has from death delivered me.

I’ll thank the LORD; now let me enter.
Unlock the gates of righteousness.
The righteous shall here be admitted,
For this indeed the LORD’s gate is.
I thank Thee, LORD, that Thou hast heard me
And rescued me from my distress.
Thou hast become, LORD, my salvation;
All those who seek Thee wilt Thou bless.

The stone the builders had rejected
Was chosen as the cornerstone.
This marv’lous act, most unexpected,
The doing is of God alone.
This is the day the LORD created;
Now let us sing with joyful tones.
Grant us prosperity, we pray Thee;
O LORD, save those who are Thine own.

Blest he who in the LORD’s name enters!
We bless you from the house of God.
He is our strength and our salvation;
The LORD has shed His light abroad.
Bind festal off’rings to the altar;
With sacrifices bring Him laud.
Shout forth your joy within His temple.
O praise the LORD, for He is God.

Thou art my God; I will extol Thee.
Thou, mighty LORD, hast rescued me.
For Thine unfailing love and mercy
I offer now my thanks to Thee.
O thank the LORD for all His goodness,
For most compassionate is He.
His steadfast grace and lovingkindness
Endure through all eternity.
359:
1. Thank the Lord; His love endures!
All to whom His love is sure,
All who fear Him day by day,
Let them thanks and praise now say!
Out of my distress I cry;
He will hear me from on high.
He will free me from all fear.
What can man do to me here?

2. For the Lord stands next to me;
He will give me victory!
Over all who hate my life
I will triumph through the strife!
In His grace I refuge find;
In His steadfast love so kind.
Trust not princes, trust not men—
Christ shall be our haven then!

3. Praise the Lord, in whose great name
All His foes I brought to shame!
Though they swarmed on ev’ry side,
In God’s name I dashed their pride.
Like a fire His judgment goes
To consume His ardent foes;
Though they pushed against me hard,
I was rescued by the Lord.

4. In the Savior we are strong,
He is all our strength and song.
To His grace now raise your voice,
In His righteousness rejoice.
For the Lord does valiantly;
We shall live eternally.
Praise His works with all your breath,
You whom He redeems from death.

5. All who know Christ’s righteousness
His great name now thank and bless.
Though His gate is righteousness,
He our saving mercy is.
Cast aside and left alone,
I have Him as cornerstone.
God has made His Son and Word
Our salvation: praise the Lord!

6. Blest are they who in His name
Come and Jesus’ grace proclaim.
God His light upon us shines
In the Savior’s sacrifice.
Praise and thanks to You, O Lord;
We extol Your living Word!
Thanks to You for You are good!
Thanks to our great loving God!
360:
1. Enter Thy courts, Thou Word of life,
My joy and peace:
Let the glad sound therein be heard;
Bid plaintive sadness cease.
Comfort my heart, Thou truth most fair;
O enter in,
Chasing despair and earthborn care,
My woe and slothful sin.

2. Glad was the time when I would sing
Thy Heav’nly praise:
Happy my heart when Thou wert nigh,
Directing all my ways.
O let Thy light, Thy joy again
Return to me:
Nor in disdain from me refrain,
Who lift my soul to Thee.

3. In Heav’n and earth Thy law endures,
Thy Word abides:
My troubled flesh trembleth in awe,
My heart in terror hides.
Yet still on Thee my hope is set:
On Thee, O Lord,
I will await and not forget
The promise of Thy Word.
361:
1. How blest the perfect in the way
Who from God’s law do not depart,
Who, holding fast the word of truth,
Seek Him with undivided heart.

2. Yea, they are kept from paths of sin
Who walk in God’s appointed way;
Thy precepts Thou hast given us
That we should faithfully obey.

3. My wav’ring heart is now resolved
Thy holy statutes to fulfill;
No more shall I be brought to shame
When I regard Thy holy will.

4. To Thee my praise sincere shall rise
When I Thy righteous judgments learn;
Forsake me not, but be my guide,
And from Thy truth I will not turn.

5. How shall the young direct their way?
What light shall be their perfect guide?
Thy Word, O Lord, will safely lead,
If in its wisdom they confide.

6. Sincerely I have sought Thee, Lord,
Oh, let me not from Thee depart;
To know Thy will and keep from sin
Thy Word I cherish in my heart.

7. O blessed LORD, teach me Thy law,
Thy righteous judgments I declare;
Thy testimonies make me glad,
For they are wealth beyond compare.

8. Upon Thy precepts and Thy ways
My heart will meditate with awe;
Thy Word shall be my chief delight,
And I will not forget Thy law.
362:
Thy servant, blest by Thee, shall live
And keep Thy Word with awe;
LORD, open Thou my eyes to see
The wonders of Thy law.

A pilgrim in the earth am I,
Thy will to me reveal;
To know Thy truth my spirit yearns,
Consumed with ardent zeal.

Thou dost rebuke the proud, O LORD,
Who hate Thy holy name;
But since I keep Thy righteous law,
Deliver me from shame.

I on Thy statutes meditate,
Though evil men deride;
Thy faithful Word is my delight,
My counselor and guide.
364:
1. Teach me, O Lord, Thy way of truth,
And from it I will not depart;
That I may steadfastly obey—
Give me an understanding heart.

2. In Thy commandments make me walk,
That in Thy law my joy shall be;
Give me a heart that loves Thy will,
From discontent and envy free.

3. Turn Thou from vanity my eyes
Let no corrupt and base design,
Nor covetous desire arise
In this unstable heart of mine.

4. Keep me from falling into sin,
Boldly may I Thy cause embrace;
Oh, may Thy Word to me again
Bring light and life and joy and peace.
365:
1. Forgive me now, O LORD and God
And let Your mercies come.
Descend from Heav’n and save me here,
According to Your mercy now,
According to Your kindly Word.

2. Then I will have an answer for
The one who brings rebuke.
My answer is my trust in You.
My enemies’ reproaching taunt
I answer with a heart of faith.

3. Take not the Word of truth from me,
That in my mouth it stays.
I hope in how You judge the world,
I keep Your law continually,
Forever and forever now.

4. And I will walk in liberty,
For in Your law I step.
I testify before great kings,
And I will never be ashamed,
Delighting in the law I love.

5. My hands are raised to Your commands,
I love to honor them.
I meditate upon Your Word,
I love to think about Your law,
And so I taste it with delight.
366:
1. May Thy mercies rest upon me,
Lord, Thy promised blessing send;
Thus I’ll tell the lost around me
Of my saving God and Friend;

2. May such words of witness never
By my life be brought to shame,
Keep me free from sin’s dominion,
Make Thy perfect will my aim.

3. May Thy promises sustain me,
Thou hast made me hope in Thee;
This my comfort in affliction—
That Thy Word has quickened me.

4. If derided by the worldling,
Still to Thy commands I’ll cleave,
And, recalling former mercies,
Help and comfort I’ll receive.

5. When the godless spurn and scorn Thee
How my anguished heart is stirred!
For on this my pilgrim journey
All my joys are from Thy Word;

6. Here I dwell on Thy perfections,
All the attributes divine;
Stores of wisdom and of knowledge
In this Word, O Lord, are mine.
367:
You, O LORD, are ev’rything I’ve longed for;
I have promised to obey Your Word.
With my whole heart I have sought Your favor;
As You promised, grant me grace, O LORD.

I have thought about my life and conduct,
And have turned my steps into Your way.
I will hasten and, without delaying,
Your commands and statutes I’ll obey.

Though the wicked with their cords ensnare me,
I will not forget instruction’s voice.
I will rise to give You thanks at midnight,
For Your righteous laws make me rejoice.

Those who fear You are my friends for ever,
All who follow in Your precepts’ way.
Earth is filled with Your great lovingkindness;
Teach me Your decrees, O LORD, I pray.
368:
Do good to Your servant, O LORD;
Be true to the Word I received.
Teach knowledge and judgment to me,
Because Your commands I’ve believed.

Before my affliction I strayed,
But now I will hold to Your Word.
You’re good and You do what is good;
Teach me Your commandments, O Lord.

Although the proud smear me with lies,
I keep Your decrees from the heart.
Their hearts are unfeeling and hard;
I love what Your precepts impart.

It’s good that I suffered distress,
So I could engraft Your commands.
Your law is more precious to me
Than silver and gold in my hands.
369:
Your hands have made and fashioned me;
Oh, make me wise, Your law to learn.
So those who fear You shall be glad
When they my hope in God discern.

LORD, You are just in all Your ways,
And faithfully You chasten me.
I beg You, let Your promised grace
Your servant’s help and comfort be.

Show mercy, Lord, that I may live,
For in Your law is all my joy.
While those who wrong me are rebuked,
Your precepts shall my thoughts employ.

Let those that fear You turn to me;
To them Your truth I will proclaim.
Instruct my heart to keep Your law,
That I may not be put to shame.
372:
1. Oh, how I love Thy law!
My teacher ev’ry day:
In all the woes of life,
My wisdom and my stay.

2. What understanding broad
Expands my willing mind:
So far beyond all else
That in this world I find.

3. How sweet the words of God,
Revealing from above
Such views of things divine,
Such grace and pow’r and love.

4. A lamp to guide my feet,
A light upon my way:
This perfect Word will I
With all my heart, obey.

5. In dangers and in trials,
Its promises I prove;
Hold fast its counsels sure
With gratitude and love.
374:
I have performed all that is right and just,
So leave me not to my oppressors’ will.
Ensure the welfare of Your servant, LORD;
Let not the insolent oppress me still.

My eyes grow weak while looking for Your aid,
While waiting for Your righteous promise, LORD;
So deal with me according to Your love,
And teach me the commandments of Your Word.

I am Your servant; give enlightenment
So that Your statutes I may understand.
O LORD, now is the time for You to act;
Your law is being broken in the land.

Because I set my heart on Your commands,
And love them more than gold, than purest gold,
And since I reckon all Your precepts right,
Each wicked path with hatred I behold.
375:
Your statutes, LORD, are wonderful,
So I obey them from my heart.
Your words, as they unfold, give light,
And truth to simple minds impart.

With open mouth I pant and yearn
To know the laws that You proclaim.
Show me the mercy You extend
To those who love and praise Your name.

Direct my footsteps in Your Word;
Let sin not hold me in its sway.
From man’s oppression set me free
That Your commands I may obey.

Upon Your servant shine Your face;
Teach me the statutes You have made.
My eyes shed streams of bitter tears
Because Your law is not obeyed.
376:
Thou, LORD, art righteous, and upright
Thine ordinances be.
Thou hast Thy testimonies right
Commanded faithfully.

My zeal consumed me; Thy commands
My adversaries spurn.
Thy promise is most pure; toward it
Thy servant loves to turn.

I’m little and despised, yet I
Thy precepts ne’er forget.
Eternal is Thy righteousness;
Thy law in truth is set.

Distress and anguish burdened me;
Great joy Thy precepts give.
Thy testimonies righteous are;
Make wise, that I may live.
377:
I call with all my heart; LORD, answer me,
And then all Your decrees I will obey.
I cry aloud to You, LORD; save my life
And I will keep Your statutes ev’ry day.

I rise before the dawn and cry for help,
For I have set my hope upon Your Word.
I stay awake throughout the hours of night,
Reflecting on Your promises, O LORD.

LORD, in Your lovingkindness hear my voice,
And in Your justice save and keep my life;
For those who disregard Your holy law
Approach with schemes of wickedness and strife.

Yet You are near to those who seek You, LORD;
All Your commands are true and ever sure.
Yes, from Your statutes long ago I learned
That You have made them always to endure.
379:
Though might y foes assail me, Lord,
I fear not them but Thee;
As boundless wealth and priceless spoil,
Thy Word rejoices me.

Deceit and falsehood I abhor,
But in Thy law delight;
Throughout the day I praise Thy name,
For all Thy ways are right.

Great peace have they who love Thy law,
Unmoved, they safely stand;
For Thy salvation I have hoped
And followed Thy command.

Thy testimonies I have kept,
They are my chief delight;
Observant of Thy law and truth,
I walk before Thy sight.
380:
Before Thee let my cry come near,
O LORD; true to Thy Word, teach me.
Before Thee let my pleading come;
True to Thy promise, rescue me.

Since Thou Thy statutes teachest me,
Oh, let my lips Thy praise confess.
Yea, of Thy Word my tongue would sing,
For Thy commands are righteousness.

Be ready with Thy hand to help,
Because Thy precepts are my choice.
I’ve longed for Thy salvation, LORD,
And in Thy holy law rejoice.

Oh, let Thine ordinances help;
My soul shall live and praise Thee yet.
A straying sheep, Thy servant, seek,
For Thy commands I ne’er forget.
381:
1. O Lord, Your law is ever sure,
Settled in heav’n, it shall endure,
Giving us strength, keeping us pure.

2. Your Word, O Lord, is my delight,
’Stablished on earth to give us light,
Teaching our hearts to know the right.

3. O Lord, Your law, like honey sweet,
And like a lamp, shall guide our feet,
Guarding our minds from sin’s deceit.

4. Your Word, O Lord, gives peace and rest,
In our afflictions and distress,
Leading to life happy and blest.
382:
I cried in trouble to the LORD,
And He has answered me.
From lying lips and crafty tongue,
O LORD, my soul set free.

What shall be given you, false tongue?
What added to your doom?
Sharp arrows of a mighty man,
And red-hot coals of broom.

Alas for me, that I sojourn
So long in Meshech’s land,
That I have made my dwelling where
The tents of Kedar stand!

Too long my soul has made its home
With those who peace abhor.
I am for peace, but when I speak
They ready are for war.
383:
In deep distress I oft have cried
To GOD, who never yet denied
To rescue me oppressed with wrongs;
Once more, O LORD, deliv’rance send,
From lying lips my soul defend,
And from the rage of sland’ring tongues.

What little profit can accrue,
And yet what heavy wrath is due,
O thou perfidious tongue, to thee?
Thy sting upon thyself shall turn;
Of lasting flames that fiercely burn,
The constant fuel thou shalt be.

But oh! how wretched is my doom,
Who am a sojourner become
In barren Mesech’s desert soil!
With Kedar’s wicked tents enclosed,
To lawless savages exposed,
Who live on nought but theft and spoil.

My hapless dwelling is with those
Who peace and amity oppose,
And pleasure take in others’ harms:
Sweet peace is all I court and seek;
But when to them of peace I speak,
They straight cry out, “To arms, to arms!”
384:
I Call on GOD in My Distress

I call on GOD in my distress,
Abandoned to His faithfulness,
And God Almighty hears me!
“LORD, save!” I cry,
“From lips that lie;
From tongues that would deceive me!”

With what reward shall you be paid?
What shall be done to you in trade?
For all your lies deserve these:
Sharp arrows sent,
From bowstrings bent,
And burning coals of broom trees!

Woe unto me, that I live hence,
In Meshech and in Kedar’s tents!
I’ve dwelt too long with uproar!
For peace I seek,
But when I speak,
They only want to wage war.
385:
I will lift up my eyes to the hills—
From whence comes my help?
My help comes from the LORD,
Who made heaven and earth.
He will not allow your foot to be moved;
He who keeps you will not slumber.
Behold, He who keeps Israel
shall neither slumber nor sleep.
The LORD is your keeper;
The LORD is your shade at your right hand.
The sun shall not strike you by day,
Nor the moon by night.
The LORD shall preserve you from all evil;
He shall preserve your soul.
The LORD shall preserve your going out and your coming in
From this time forth, and even forevermore.
386:
I to the hills will lift mine eyes;
From whence doth come mine aid?
My safety cometh from the LORD,
Who heav’n and earth hath made.

Thy foot He’ll not let slide, nor will
He slumber that thee keeps.
Behold, He that keeps Israel,
He slumbers not, nor sleeps.

The LORD thee keeps, the LORD thy shade
On thy right hand doth stay:
The moon by night thee shall not smite,
Nor yet the sun by day.

The LORD shall keep thy soul; He shall
Preserve thee from all ill.
Henceforth thy going out and in
God keep for ever will.
387:
Unto the hills around do I lift up
My longing eyes:
Oh, whence for me shall my salvation come,
From whence arise?
From God the LORD doth come my certain aid,
From God the LORD who heav’n and earth hath made.

He will not suffer that thy foot be moved,
Safe shalt thou be;
No careless slumber shall His eyelids close
Who keepeth thee.
Behold He sleepeth not,
He slumb’reth ne’er,
Who keepeth Israel in His holy care.

Jehovah is Himself thy keeper true;
Thy changeless shade
Jehovah, evermore on thy right hand,
Himself hath made;
And thee no sun by day shall ever smite,
No moon shall harm thee in the silent night.

From ev’ry evil shall He keep thy soul,
From ev’ry sin;
Jehovah shall preserve thy going out,
Thy coming in;
Above thee watching, He whom we adore
Shall keep thee henceforth, yea, for evermore.
388:
Oh, ’twas a joyful sound to hear
Our tribes devoutly say,
Up, Israel, to the temple haste,
And keep your festal day.

At Salem’s courts we must appear,
With our assembled pow’rs,
In strong and beauteous order ranged,
Like her united tow’rs.

’Tis thither by divine command,
The tribes of God repair,
Before His ark to celebrate
His name with praise and pray’r.

Tribunals stand erected there,
Where equity takes place;
There stand the courts and palaces
Of royal David’s race.

Oh, pray we then for Salem’s peace,
For they shall prosp’rous be,
(Thou holy city of our God!)
Who bear true love to thee.

May peace within thy sacred walls
A constant guest be found;
With plenty and prosperity
Thy palaces be crowned.

For my dear brethren’s sake, and friends
No less than brethren dear,
I’ll pray— May peace in Salem’s tow’rs
A constant guest appear.

But most of all I’ll seek thy good,
And ever wish thee well,
For Zion and the temple’s sake,
Where God vouchsafes to dwell.
389:
I was glad when they said to me,
“Let us go into the house of the LORD.”
Our feet have been standing
within your gates, O Jerusalem!
Jerusalem is built
as a city that is compact together,
Where the tribes go up,
The tribes of the LORD,
To the Testimony of Israel,
To give thanks to the name of the LORD.
For thrones are set there for judgment,
The thrones of the house of David.
Pray for the peace of Jerusalem:
“May they prosper who love you.
Peace be within your walls,
Prosperity within your palaces.”
For the sake of my brethren and companions,
I will now say, “Peace be within you.”
Be cause of the house of the LORD our God
I will seek your good.
390:
I was filled with joy and gladness
When they said with one accord,
“Let us make our pilgrim journey
To the house of God the LORD.”
O Jerus’lem, O Jerus’lem,
We are standing in your gates.

As a city bound together
Is Jerusalem designed.
There, by law, the tribes ascending
Thank the LORD in praise combined.
Thrones of David, Thrones of David,
There for royal justice stand.

Pray for peace, the peace of Zion:
“Prosper those who love you well!
Peace be in your walls forever;
Safety in your towers dwell!”
Peace and safety, Peace and safety
In Jerusalem abound.

For the sake of my companions,
For my brothers, I will say:
“May God’s peace abide within you!”
For the temple’s sake I pray.
For the LORD’s house, For the LORD’s house,
I will ever seek your good.
391:
1. To You we lift our eyes,
O God enthroned above!
With longing gaze and heaving sighs
We plead Your love!

2. As servants strain to see
Their earthly lord’s command,
So we would in Your presence be
And firmly stand!

3. Have mercy, Lord, we pray;
Our souls are weary, worn.
The wicked world condemns our way
And heaps up scorn.

4. Our souls are sore oppressed
By this world’s ease and pride.
In You we would be healed and blest,
And in You hide.
392:
To Thee, O Lord who dwellest in the height,
My eyes look up for light.
Lo, as the eyes of servants, when neglected,
Are to their lord directed,
And as a maiden’s glance for favor lingers
Upon her mistress’ fingers,
Thus, too, our eyes look to our Master’s face
Till He provide us grace.

O LORD our God, grant us Thy grace again,
Grant us Thy grace again,
For lo, our ears are full of man’s derision
At our estranged condition;
Our soul is sated with the scorn and chiding
Of those at ease abiding,
And of the proud who in their vanity
Regard us haughtily.
393:
To You enthroned in Heaven,
To You we turn our eye,
Like servants with their master,
As maids to mistress sigh.
To You we look, O LORD God,
Our Master in the heav’ns,
Until You give us mercy,
Until our hardship ends.

Have mercy on us, LORD God,
Your mercy to us send,
For we have known contempt, Lord,
Derision without end.
Our souls are overburdened
By scorn of those at ease,
Who heap contempt upon us
While doing as they please.

Have mercy on us, LORD God,
Have mercy without end.
Look down on us in pity,
Your great compassion send.
Our eyes look to You only,
For mercy and release.
You are the Lord Most Holy;
In mercy, give us peace.
394:
If God had not been on our side
And had not come to aid us,
The foes with all their pow’r and pride
Would surely have dismayed us;
For we, His flock, would have to fear
The threat of man both far and near
Who rise in might against us.

Their furious wrath, did God permit,
Would surely have consumed us,
And as a deep and yawning pit,
With life and limb entombed us.
Like men o’er whom dark waters roll
Their wrath would have engulfed our soul
And, like a flood o’erwhelmed us.

Blest be the Lord, who foiled their threat
That they could not devour us;
Our souls, like birds, escaped their net,
They could not overpow’r us.
The snare is broken— we are free!
Our help is ever, Lord, in Thee,
Who madest earth and heaven.
395:
Had not the LORD, may Israel say,
Been pleased to interpose;
Had He not then espoused our cause,
When men against us rose;

Their wrath had swallowed us alive,
And raged without control:
Their spite and pride’s united floods
Had quite o’erwhelmed our soul.

But praised be our eternal Lord,
Who rescued us that day,
Nor to their savage jaws gave up
Our threatened lives a prey.

Our soul is like a bird escaped
From out the fowler’s net;
The snare is broke, their hopes are crossed,
And we at freedom set.

Secure in His almighty name,
Our confidence remains,
Who, as He made both heav’n and earth,
Of both sole monarch reigns.
396:
Let Israel now say in thankfulness
That if the LORD had not our right maintained
And if the LORD had not with us remained
When cruel men against us rose to strive,
We’d surely have been swallowed up alive.

2. Yea, when their wrath against us fiercely rose,
Then would the tide o’er us have spread its wave;
The raging stream would have become our grave;
The surging flood, in proudly swelling roll,
Most surely would have overwhelmed us all.

Blest be the LORD who made us not their prey;
As from the fowler’s net a bird may flee,
So from their broken snare did we go free.
Our only help is in God’s holy name;
He made the earth and all the heav’nly frame.
397:
Like Zion’s steadfast mount are they
Who in the LORD confide;
Secure, immovable they stand,
Forever to abide,
Forever to abide.

As round about Jerusalem
The mountains give defense,
Jehovah is His people’s guard,
Their lasting confidence,
Their lasting confidence.

No tyrant’s scepter o’er the good
Shall undisturbed abide,
Lest righteous men, oppressed by wrong,
To evil turn aside,
To evil turn aside.

O Thou Jehovah, to the good
Thy goodness now impart,
Thy lovingkindness show to them
That upright are in heart,
That upright are in heart.

All those that turn from righteousness
With wayward, wand’ring feet,
With sinners GOD will lead them forth,
The sinner’s doom to meet,
The sinner’s doom to meet.

6.  O Thou who art Thy people’s shield,
Their helper and their guide,
Upon them let Thy grace and peace
For evermore abide,
For evermore abide.
398:
Those who trust in the LORD are like Mount Zion,
Which cannot be moved, but abides forever.
As the mountains surround Jerusalem,
So the LORD surrounds His people
From this time forth and forever.
For the scepter of wickedness shall not rest
On the land allotted to the righteous,
Lest the righteous reach out their hands to iniquity.
Do good, O LORD, to those who are good,
And to those who are upright in their hearts.
As for such as turn aside to their crooked ways,
The LORD shall lead them away with the workers of iniquity.
Peace be upon Israel!
399:
They in the LORD that firmly trust
Shall be like Zion hill,
Which at no time can be removed,
But standeth ever still.

As round about Jerusalem
The mountains ever stand,
The LORD His people doth surround,
And evermore defend.

For tyrant’s rod upon the lot
Of just men shall not lie;
Lest righteous men stretch forth their hands
To work iniquity.

Do Thou to all those who are good
Thy goodness, LORD, impart;
And also do Thou good to them
Who upright are in heart.

But as for such as turn aside
In their own crooked way,
God shall lead forth with wicked men:
On Israel peace shall stay.
400:
Like Zion’s mountain shall they be
Who in the LORD confide,
A mount which never can be moved
But ever shall abide.

As all around Jerusalem
The mountains firmly stand.
The LORD for evermore surrounds
The people of His hand.

Upon the land of righteous ones
No evil rule shall press,
Lest righteous ones put forth their hands
To work unrighteousness.

O LORD, to all those who are good
Show Yourself good and kind,
And likewise show Your goodness to
All them of upright mind.

Yet shall the LORD drive out all those
In crooked ways who dwell,
Along with all who practice sin;
But peace on Israel!
401:
When in His might the LORD
Arose to set us free,
And Zion was restored
From her captivity,
In transports then of joy and mirth
We praised the LORD of all the earth.

2.  The nations saw with fear
The might of God displayed,
When He at last drew near
To give His people aid;
Great things for us the LORD has wrought,
And gladness to our hearts has brought.

Again refresh us, LORD,
With Thy reviving love,
And be Thy blessing poured
In mercy from above;
By grace revive our hearts again,
As streams refreshed by copious rain.

Although with bitter tears
The sower bears his seed,
When harvest time appears
He shall be glad indeed;
For they that in the sowing weep
Shall yet in joy and gladness reap.
402:
When Zion’s fortunes GOD restored,
It was a dream come true.
Our mouths were then with laughter filled,
Our tongues with songs anew.

2. The nations said, “The LORD has done
Great things for Israel.”
The LORD did mighty things for us,
And joy our hearts knew well.

Restore our fortunes, gracious LORD,
Like streams in desert soil.
A joyful harvest will reward
The weeping sower’s toil.

The man who, bearing seed to sow,
Goes out with tears of grief,
Will come again with songs of joy,
Bearing his harvest sheaf.
403:
We were like people in a dream
When GOD set Zion free;
We laughed, we sang, our voices rang
With shouts of liberty.

2. The heathen nations ’round us said,
“God’s gifts to them are good!”
Yes, God has done great things for us,
We praise Him as we should.

Restore our fortunes now, O Lord,
Like desert waterways,
And grant that those who sow in tears
May reap with hymns of praise.

Let those who weep as they go out
And take with them the seed
Come back in joy with harvest sheaves
Fulfilling all their need.
404:
Unless the LORD the House Shall Build

Unless the LORD the house shall build,
The weary builders toil in vain;
Unless the LORD the city shield,
The guards a useless watch maintain.

In vain you rise ere morning break,
And late your nightly vigils keep,
And bread of anxious care partake;
God gives to His beloved sleep.

Lo, children are a gift of God,
And sons the blessing He commands;
These, when in youthful days bestowed,
Are like the shafts in warrior’s hands.

And happy they whose quivers bear
Full store of arrows such as these;
They in the gate are free from fear,
And boldly face their enemies.
405:
Except the LORD build the house,
They labor in vain that build it.
Except the LORD keep the city,
The watchman waketh but in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early,
To sit up late,
To eat the bread of sorrows,
For so He giveth His beloved sleep.
Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD,
And the fruit of the womb is His reward.
As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man,
So are children of the youth.
Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them;
They shall not be ashamed,
But they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.
406:
If GOD does not build up the house,
The builders labor but in vain.
If God the LORD does not stand guard,
Your city watchmen cannot save.
Early to work and late to rest
Will profit you but weariness.

2. The LORD restores His folk with sleep.
God gives us children to make sure
That godly parents shall be spared
When adversaries crowd the door.
Strong sons and daughters raised in faith
Become like arrows from the LORD.
407:
Except the LORD build the house, they labor in vain that build it:
Except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain.
It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so He giveth His beloved sleep.
Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is His reward.
As arrows are in the hand of a mighty man, so are children of the youth.
Happy is the man that hath his quiver full of them:
They shall not be ashamed, but they shall speak with the enemies in the gate.
408:
Blest is the man who fears the LORD,
And who in faith obeys His Word:
The one who walks upon His way,
He will in favor with God stay.

The man who works hard with his hands,
And only eats off his own lands,
He will be happy and will grow,
Who only reaps what he did sow.

His wife will always faithful be,
His children life and strength shall see,
The man who fears the LORD is blest,
And God will give him peace and rest.

For in his life no wars will be,
And he, his children’s sons shall see.
In Israel there would be great peace,
If only godly men increased.
409:
Blest is ev’ryone who fears the LORD;
Blest is ev’ryone who walks in His ways.
You shall savor all your work’s reward,
And it shall be well with you all your days.
May the LORD bless you, bless you from Zion,
Prosper your hands and give you life!
May you live to see your children’s children—
Peace for the people of His delight!

Loved ones flourishing within your house,
Children planted in the way of truth.
These are blessings for the man who vows
To worship the LORD and fear Him too!
May the LORD bless you, bless you from Zion,
Prosper your hands and give you life!
May you live to see your children’s children—
Peace for the people of His delight!
410:
1. Blest the man that fears Jehovah
And that walketh in His ways;
Thou shalt eat of thy hands’ labor
And be prospered all thy days.
Like a vine with fruit abounding
In thy house thy wife is found,
And like olive plants thy children,
Compassing thy table ’round,
And like olive plants thy children,
Compassing thy table ’round.

2. Lo, on him that fears Jehovah
Shall this blessedness attend,
For Jehovah out of Zion
Shall to thee His blessing send.
Thou shalt see Jerus’lem prosper
All thy days till life shall cease;
Thou shalt see thy children’s children.
Unto Israel be peace!
Thou shalt see thy children’s children.
Unto Israel be peace!
411:
How blest are all who fear the LORD,
And walk in all His ways!
You’ll eat your labor’s fruit, be blest,
And prosper in your days.

Your wife will as a fruitful vine
Within your house be found;
Your children will as olive plants
Your table gather round.

Behold, thus shall the man be blest
Who truly fears the LORD!
The LORD from Zion grant to you
His blessing and reward.

4. And may you see Jerus’lem’s good
All days on earth you dwell.
May you your children’s children see,
And peace on Israel.
412:
“They Often Hurt Me From My Youth”

“They often hurt me from my youth,”
Let Israel now repeat it—
“They often hurt me from my youth,
Yet they have not succeeded.
The plowmen plowed upon my back.”
The righteous LORD broke their attack;
He cut their cords in pieces.

Let Zion’s foes be turned in shame.
Like rooftop grass is rootless,
Which withers on the day it came;
The reaper finds it fruitless.
When binding sheaves, he turns away.
The men who pass them never say,
“We pray the LORD would bless you.”
413:
From my youth up, may Israel say,
They oft have me assailed,
Reduced me oft to heavy straits,
But never quite prevailed.

Oft have they plowed my patient back
With furrows deep and long;
My righteous God has broke the chains,
And rescued me from wrong.

Defeat, confusion, shameful rout,
Are still the doom of those,
Their righteous doom, who Zion hate,
And Zion’s God oppose.

Like grass upon the housetop wilts,
Untimely let them fade,
Which too much heat, and want of root,
Has blasted in the blade,

Which in his arms no reaper takes,
But unregarded leaves;
Nor binder thinks it worth his pains
To fold it into sheaves.

No traveler that passes by,
Vouch safes a minute’s stop,
To give it one kind look, or crave
God’s blessing on the crop.
414:
1. Up from my youth, may Israel say,
Have I been nursed in tears;
My griefs were constant as the day,
And tedious as the years.

2. Up from my youth I bore the rage
Of all the sons of strife;
Oft they assailed my riper age,
But not destroyed my life.

3. Their cruel plow had torn my flesh
With furrows long and deep;
Hourly they vexed my wounds afresh,
Nor let my sorrows sleep.

4. The Lord grew angry on His throne,
And, with impartial eye,
Measured the mischiefs they had done,
Then let His arrows fly.

5. How was their insolence surprised
To hear His thunders roll!
And all the foes of Zion seized
With horror to the soul!

6. Thus shall the men that hate the saints
Be blasted from the sky;
Their glory fades, their courage faints
And all their projects die.

7. What though they flourish tall and fair,
They have no root beneath;
Their growth shall perish in despair,
